title: Dependency Triage Workbench — conflict scoring, ownership handoff, and auto-escalation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Cross-team roadmap blockers are discovered too late in the cycle and lack consistent ownership or urgency signals. Several recent cutovers (Dedicated autoscaler launch, Private upgrade path) were delayed by misrouted dependency handoffs and unclear rollback owners.

Goal: Ship a lightweight 'Dependency Triage Workbench' in the Console and an accompanying API that surface live blocker signals, calculate a conflict score, and provide one-click ownership handoff or escalation. The workbench should reduce cycle-level dependency resolution time by 30% and eliminate >50% of last-week-of-release firefights driven by cross-team miscommunication.

Scope: MVP includes (1) conflict scoring engine (weighting by timeline proximity, severity, owner response time), (2) a triage UI for PMs/EMs to reassign ownership or request design/security intervention, (3) Slack + email notifications for high-severity conflicts, (4) an API for Eng/Design/Infra to push readiness updates, and (5) basic audit log entries for handoffs. No RBAC or per-customer data plane integration in MVP — those are follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: A conflict score is computed for each roadmap dependency and is visible in the workbench UI
PMs/EMs can reassign ownership from the workbench and a log entry is created
High-severity conflicts trigger a configurable channel alert (Slack) and an auto-created incident placeholder in our tracking board
Teams can submit readiness updates via API and those updates adjust the conflict score in near-real time
Dashboard KPI: mean dependency resolution time decreases by 30% in pilot orgs within first month
updates: 2026-02-20 — Ticket created by Maya Chen. Initial problem statement and success metrics added. Asked Eng to prototype scoring rules with sample data.

2026-02-25 — Sync with Eng (Ravi Patel) and Design (Amira Solis). Agreed on three scoring signals: timeline proximity, owner response latency, and cross-functional criticality. Design to produce two compact UI sketches for a side-panel workbench.

2026-03-01 — Eng spike completed: prototype scoring service that consumes existing roadmap events and calculates a numeric score (0-100). Proof-of-concept shows most current blockers land between 55-85 scores. Recorded compute cost estimate for continuous scoring: low (batch every 5m).

2026-03-04 — Design sketch v1 uploaded to Figma. Lean layout chosen: list view + detail pane + quick-assign dropdown. Accessibility review flagged color contrast for severity badges; Design to revise.

2026-03-08 — Security review intake: SEC requested audit-log schema and retention policy. Added SEC-19 to dependencies. No major blockers, but note: high-severity alerts must redact customer identifiers in public channels.

2026-03-10 — Implemented Slack alert prototype in #roadmap-triage with test webhook. Initial feedback: alerts useful but noisy; add rate-limit and dedupe window. Added to scope as configurable parameter.

2026-03-12 — PM review: prioritized API schema changes for readiness updates. Decided to scope RBAC & org-scoped permissions to follow-up sprint. Updated due date to 2026-04-01 for MVP pilot rollout to two internal product teams.
next_steps: Finalize scoring weights and edge-case rules (rush windows, holiday blackout) with Eng by 2026-03-15
Design to deliver accessible high-contrast badges and quick-assign dropdown by 2026-03-17
Eng to build API contract and wire up readiness update endpoint (spec in GitHub PR) by 2026-03-22
Set up pilot with two product teams and baseline current dependency MTTR before rollout (Owners: Maya + Lucas)
Create runbook for auto-escalation and dedupe logic and hand to SRE/Oncall for sign-off
risks: False positives from scoring may create alert fatigue. Slack alerts could expose PII unless redaction is enforced. Teams need cultural adoption (must agree to update readiness status) — without that, scores will be inaccurate. Mitigations: start with internal pilot, add dedupe/rate-limit, enforce redaction rules in alerts, instrument adoption metrics.
